gaps.sentence: The crowd waited ___ for the gates to open (PATIENT).
gaps.explanation: An adverb modifies the verb 'waited': patiently. 'Patients' are people in hospital.

gaps.sentence: In my opinion, that restaurant is ___ — the food is nothing special (RATE).
gaps.explanation: 'Nothing special' shows the restaurant is praised too much: overrated (over- + rated).

gaps.hint: noun needed after 'His'; note the -al suffix
gaps.explanation: The noun of 'refuse' is 'refusal' (-al noun); 'refuse' as a noun means rubbish.

gaps.sentence: He ___ forgets to bring the tickets, as usual (TYPICAL).
gaps.hint: adverb of frequency needed to modify 'forgets' (-ly)
gaps.explanation: An adverb modifies the verb 'forgets': typically means in the usual way.

gaps.hint: noun needed after 'signs of'; note the spelling change
gaps.explanation: After 'signs of' a noun is needed: recovery (the -er of 'recover' becomes -ery).

gaps.sentence: He had a happy ___ in the countryside (CHILD).
gaps.hint: noun needed: the period of being a child (-hood)
gaps.explanation: The suffix -hood forms period-of-life nouns: childhood.

gaps.sentence: It was the most ___ (FORGET) trip of my life.
gaps.hint: negative adjective: too good to forget
gaps.explanation: 'Unforgettable' = impossible to forget; 'forgetful' describes a person who forgets.

gaps.sentence: The new bypass will be ___ (BENEFIT) to thousands of commuters.
gaps.explanation: 'Be beneficial to' — the adjective follows the verb 'be'.
